# Backend model files

`backend/model/*.json` is the backend metadata inventory and source of truth; `backend/reports/*.sql` is the source-owned SQL surface referenced by Report model items. The Blueprint Ledger under `domain/` and everything under `.domainry/` are CLI-owned projections that `model apply` converges from those sources. Never edit `domain/**`, rendered Blueprints, or `.domainry/**` by hand, and never treat them as an authoring input.

## File contract

Every file under `backend/model/` matching `*.json` is loaded, in lexical filename order:

```json
{
  "contract_version": "domainry-backend-model-v1",
  "items": [
    {
      "module": "project",
      "kind": "project",
      "key": "project",
      "payload": {"blueprint": {"schema_version": "1", "id": "gym", "name": "Gym", "description": "Gym operations"}}
    },
    {
      "module": "membership",
      "kind": "actor_role",
      "key": "membership-roles",
      "requirement_keys": ["membership-management"],
      "depends_on": ["project/project/project"],
      "payload": {"emits": []}
    }
  ]
}
```

Item fields:

- `module`, `kind`, `key` — required identity. `kind` is one of `project`, `requirement`, `actor_role`, `object_relation`, `action_authorization`, `workflow_connector`, `acceptance`, `resource`. Identity segments are stable lowercase keys; the unique project item is always `project/project/project`.
- `status` — optional, `closed` (default) or `decision_required`; `decision_required` must match at least one unresolved decision.
- `requirement_keys`, `depends_on`, `decisions` — optional arrays (default empty). `depends_on` entries are full `module/kind/key` addresses.
- `payload` — the item body (default `{}`), identical to the Ledger item payload contract for that kind.

One `module/kind/key` may be declared exactly once across all model files. Group items by owning module — typically one file per module (`backend/model/<module>.json`). Do not add envelope fields (`contract_version`, `module`, `kind`, `key`) inside `payload`, and do not nest `status`, `requirement_keys`, `depends_on`, or `decisions` there.

## Requirement payload

A `requirement` item's `payload.requirement` carries the requirement statement plus its `behaviors[]` array of behavior-owner tuples (owner, resource_key, and the tuple fields defined in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md)). An empty `behaviors` array is legal only when the payload also supplies a non-empty `no_executable_behavior_reason` string explaining why the requirement owns no executable behavior (for example, purely declarative authorization/navigation policy carried by roles, data permissions, and views). The field must be absent when `behaviors` is non-empty; `model validate` fails closed on both violations (`empty behaviors require a reason` / `ledger.requirement_incomplete`).

For `object_sql_v1`, use exactly one project-owned SQL file named after the Report key instead of embedding a large escaped SQL string. Replace only the `sql` member with `"sql_file":"backend/reports/<report-key>.sql"`. `model validate|plan|apply` requires that exact canonical project-relative regular file, rejects symlinks/traversal and simultaneous `sql` + `sql_file`, normalizes line endings and a final newline, records its SHA-256 in the apply receipt, and embeds the normalized SQL into the existing published Runtime contract. `sql_file` is not a Runtime field or a query DSL; Runtime still receives `object_sql_v1.sql`, and `model export` may therefore emit the compatible inline form.

## Commands

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model preflight        --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model validate --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan     --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model apply    --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module> [--environment <name> | --service <url>] [--allow-destructive] [--sync-only] [--evolution-audit-sha256 <emitted-sha256> --evolution-reason <reviewed-reason>]
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model export   --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--force]
```

- `preflight` is the authoritative no-HTTP, local-read-only repair loop. It reuses the same model/SQL loader, strict item contract, Ledger graph, in-process authoring checks, deterministic Project Contract projector, and Runtime-manifest compiler as the formal path. It atomically replaces `.domainry/builder/disposable/model-preflight-result.json` for both `valid` and `repair_required`; stdout contains only `state`, `issue_count`, the project-relative artifact locator, SHA-256, and identity. A repair result exits non-zero. Read the artifact from the first Gate run and batch-repair it; do not rerun a failed Gate merely to obtain diagnostics and do not implement a bespoke `jq`/regex preflight. This local boundary does not claim live Plane, Runtime configuration, provider, database, or scenario checks.
- `validate` parses every model file, enforces the item contract, and reports the pending plan counts without writing model/Ledger state.
- `plan` additionally lists the exact item IDs classified as create, update, or delete.
- `apply` is the single release command: it converges the Ledger to the model files, gates on the aggregated metadata checklist, then chains live validation, signed publication, dependency resolution, backend materialization/evolution, and source finalization, stopping at the first failing stage. Every release apply resolves the dependency seed in staging before it installs files or writes a successful materialization receipt; a resolution failure stops closed and must be repaired before another round. For an existing Builder delivery change, the first run emits `evolution_review_required` plus an audit path and SHA-256. Inspect the immutable audit and run the same product command through a new round-specific Gate with that exact emitted SHA-256 and a concrete review reason; never calculate or substitute the hash. After any other failure, repair the model files (or the reported stage input) and use a new Gate for the next command run. stdout carries one compact summary; the complete receipt is written to `.domainry/builder/model-apply.json`. `--sync-only` stops after the Ledger sync and checklist for local iteration without a Domainry Plane target.
- `export` bootstraps model files from the current Ledger (one file per module) for a project created before this workflow; it refuses to overwrite existing model files without `--force`.

CAS identities, batch contexts, and Ledger journals are handled entirely inside the CLI. Never compute, copy, or supply a SHA-256 by hand, and never call Domainry Plane directly or reconstruct its request signing.

## Convergence and safety rules

`plan`/`apply` classify every declared item against the current Ledger:

- **create / update** — applied automatically and atomically; an unchanged item is never rewritten.
- **delete** — an item present in the Ledger but absent from the model is destructive. `apply` refuses and names the missing items until the model restores them or the run explicitly passes `--allow-destructive`.
- A **rename** of `module`, `kind`, or `key` is a delete plus a create. Treat renames as destructive: confirm data expectations first, then apply with explicit consent.
- The model owns definitions only. Runtime instance data — business records, sessions, credentials, user-role assignments made at runtime — is never compared or mutated by convergence.

Complete each module's full inventory (Objects, Relations, Actions, Roles, authorization, data scopes, Workflows, state machines, Reports, Schedulers, Automations, Connectors, seeds, acceptance) before the first `model validate`; do not validate a partial inventory and do not use `validate` or `apply` as a resource-by-resource schema probe. Immediately before the first validation, perform one cross-resource preflight over the whole draft: ownership closes **both ways** (every requirement behavior resolves to its resource, and every emitted Action/Workflow/Scheduler/Automation — including export/audit helper Actions — has one matching behavior owner); every Action's allowed roles have the required object access plus reads of every declared project relation target; Identity bootstrap/demo-user/profile references resolve; every frontend entrypoint object exists; Report SQL paths equal `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`; export controls resolve their Report, Action, audit/download Objects, mappings, and one role's complete grant chain; every declared Object has a valid seed; and acceptance actors, roles, operations, positive cases, and denial cases resolve. Run validation only after this inventory is closed. On failure, collect and repair the complete diagnostic set and re-run once; do not revalidate after each local edit. Once validation returns `state:"valid"`, keep that model immutable while attaching evidence. Any requirement-backed edit invalidates the result and starts a new atomic `validate` + `plan` cycle. After a failed apply, fix the complete finding set in the files and re-run once.

**Initial/default-state closure is part of that single preflight.** For every explicit requirement or accepted evidence statement that names an initial or default field value, author the value as the owning `objects[].fields[].default_value`. This is mandatory when the Object is exposed through generic Runtime create (including `entrypoints[].create_objects` or a role's `<object>.create` permission); acceptance prose, a seed, a frontend form default, or an Action input constant is not metadata default behavior. Mechanically verify that every select default matches its stable field option vocabulary and every state-field default matches both that vocabulary and the owning `state_machines[].states`. If the requirement does not identify an initial/default value, do not invent one merely to satisfy prose; record only the deterministic behavior the accepted demand actually establishes.

Before that first validation, apply this strict nested-shape card; these objects reject aliases and convenient prose fields:

- `identity_bootstrap.menus[]` uses `id`, `key`, `label`, optional `description`/`route`/`icon`/`parent_id`, and required `sort_order` plus `status`; there is no `surface`. Bind roles with one row per pair, `role_menus:[{"role_id":"technician","menu_id":"menu_my_work"}]`, or with `role_menu_sets:[{"role_id":"technician","menu_ids":["menu_my_work"]}]`; never use `role_key`, `menu_keys`, or a grouped object under `role_menus`.
- Object field `validation` uses the exact Blueprint keys `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `options`, and `target`; `minimum`/`maximum` are Runtime authoring API names, not Blueprint JSON fields.
- Every `expected_reports[].metrics` value is an array; use `[]` when the scenario asserts execution/export but no metric values. It is never an object map.
- A Report emission repeats its identity inside the value: `{"collection":"reports","key":"part_usage_report","value":{"key":"part_usage_report",...}}`. The envelope `key` does not populate `value.key`; omitting the inner key makes `sql_file` resolve against an empty report key. The two keys must be identical.
- For `object_sql_v1`, each SQL `JOIN ... AS <alias>` has exactly one `join_cardinalities` entry shaped `{"alias":"<alias>","cardinality":"many_to_one"}` (or another truthful supported cardinality). It has only `alias` and `cardinality`; never use `left_alias`/`right_alias` there. Those names belong to Dataset join definitions, not Object SQL cardinality declarations.
- `report_export_controls[]` is closed to the fields listed in [reports](capabilities/reports.md). Do not invent requester/scope convenience properties; requester scoping is enforced by the declared grant chain and record mapping.
- `object_sql_v1` SQL has explicit `ORDER BY` and a literal business-bounded `LIMIT` in the inclusive range `1..10000`; the Blueprint `limit` diagnostic refers to SQL text, not a JSON `limit` property. Never use a larger placeholder such as `LIMIT 100000`.

Business menu definitions and role-menu assignments are **not emitted collections**. They are deterministic project bootstrap facts under the single project-level `identity_bootstrap` object. When acceptance names `effective_menu_list`, declare the needed `identity_bootstrap.menus` and either `role_menus` or `role_menu_sets` before apply; authoring rejects a probed role with no binding. Do not postpone that acceptance prerequisite to a manual post-apply step. Runtime's Identity menu management API remains the supported path for later operational edits; updates keep their normal schema-hash CAS contract.

`identity_bootstrap` (departments, organization scopes/memberships, workforce profiles/assignments, menus and role-menu bindings) is **not** an emits collection — an emitted collection always renders as an array and fails `schema.type: expected object`. It is a single project-level Blueprint property: declare it inside the **project item's `payload.blueprint.identity_bootstrap`** as `{"version":"1","departments":[{"id":"east","name":"East"}],"menus":[{"id":"menu_my_work","key":"my_work","label":"My work","route":"business.my_work","sort_order":10,"status":"active"}],"role_menus":[{"role_id":"technician","menu_id":"menu_my_work"}]}`. `version` is the **string** constant `"1"` (integer `1` fails `schema.const`). `demo_users[].department_id` must reference a department `id` declared there (`identity.user_department_not_found` otherwise).

`demo_users[].profile_bindings` is the single owner of a demo user's business-profile link. Its referenced profile seed must leave the profile extension's `identity_relation_field` absent; do not also write a user ID into that seed field. `model validate` rejects the two-owner form as `identity.user_profile_seed_relation_owned_twice`, before Runtime bootstrap. Runtime still converges the exact pre-existing same-user link idempotently for older valid deliveries, but a different-user replacement remains a conflict.

Two more Action/role rules the validator enforces:

- **Every project-owned Handler Action — including scheduler-driven bulk handlers — must declare at least one required payload field in `idempotency_keys`** (`ledger.action_idempotency_required`). A scheduled job's invocation payload carries the key (e.g. a required `run_date` bound from the trigger event).
- **Multiple `data_permissions[]` entries for the same object do NOT merge**: the validator reads one entry's `read`/`write` per object, so "read=department + write=own" cannot be expressed as two entries (`ledger.action_role_data_permission_required` reports the losing entry's booleans). Declare a single entry with the union capability and enforce the narrower write constraint through a before-update automation assert on the owner, a Handler precondition, or CRUD permission removal.

## Single ownership

Every rendered resource key has exactly one originating model item. A `ledger.resource_duplicate` diagnostic means a second item attempted to emit an existing resource; it is never an overlay or merge mechanism. Repair it in the model files: remove the duplicate declaration and extend the item that already owns the resource. For example, a missing permission on an emitted role belongs in the item that already emits the role, not in a new `actor_role` item emitting the same role key.

Every behavior `resource_key` must resolve to the concrete resource owned by that behavior; the exact owner-to-emitted-collection mapping and resource-key rules live in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md) — do not guess a collection from prose.

Agent metadata is resource-owned in the same model: emit `skills`, `agents`, `agent_tasks`, `agent_service_principals`, and `agent_entrypoints` from separate `resource` items in dependency order, each linked to the requirement it satisfies. Never place these collections inside the project item. Read [Agents and Agent Tasks](capabilities/agents-and-agent-tasks.md) before authoring them; exact fields and references come from the live Blueprint Definition consumed by `model validate|plan|apply`.

## Action declarations

An emitted `actions[]` entry requires `key`, `name`, `object_key`, `kind`, and `audit_event`. `kind` is the closed enum `bulk_operation`, `conditional_update`, `object_create`, `object_operation`, `record_delete`, `record_operation`, `record_restore`, `record_update`, or `transition_state`.

**Kind selection for Handler Actions**: a project-owned Handler must NOT use kind `object_create` — that kind carries the system `record.create` owner, and an Action with both a system operation and a business handler owner is rejected at **Runtime bootstrap** ("action has both system operation record.create and business handler owners"); no static stage (validate/finalize/check/verify/package) catches it. Use **`object_operation`** for an object-level Handler command (creation included) and **`record_operation`** for a record-targeted one; a Handler that creates records does the create through its data capabilities.

Authorization splits by ownership and both halves are enforced at compile time (`ledger.runtime_manifest_invalid`):

- A **project-owned Handler Action** (one that declares `handler`) uses the `authorization` block (`allowed_roles`, …).
- A **system Action** (`transition_state` and every other non-Handler kind) must instead declare `permission` — it compiles to Runtime `requires_permission`. `authorization` is rejected on a system Action, and a missing `permission` is rejected too. Runtime executes a system Action for any role holding that permission, so a role that must not execute a guarded transition (for example, "only managers close") must not hold the declared permission — or the transition must be owned by a manager-only Handler Action instead.
- **The `permission` key must be exactly two dot-segments: `<object_key>.<suffix>`** (e.g. `ticket.transition_close`, not `ticket.transition.close`). Runtime authorization re-derives the check as `<action.object_key>.<last-segment>`, so a three-segment key like `ticket.transition.start` passes `model validate` and one authorization layer but is re-read as the never-granted `ticket.start` by the second — every legitimate caller then fails with 403 `backend.permission.denied` at runtime. Platform permission keys granted verbatim in `roles[].permissions` (e.g. `identity.audit.view`) are exact-match strings and are not subject to this rule; it binds project-declared Action `permission` values and object CRUD keys.

Acceptance scenarios are strict Blueprint resources, not free-form test notes. Use only the declared top-level fields `key`, `name`, `description`, `actor`, `role`, `role_key`, `seed_data`, `seed_records`, `actions`, `attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_outcome`, `expected_error_code`, `expected_records`, `expected_reports`, `assertions`, and `config`; never invent shortcuts such as `objects` or `attempted_objects`. Express record/RLS expectations through `expected_records` or typed `assertions`.

`workflows` means a positive **manual** Workflow invocation and therefore requires `trigger_contract.type:"manual"`. Do not list `scheduled`, `action_completed`, or `record_event` Workflows there: the finalizer attributes them to their real trigger owner (the matching `scheduled_jobs`, Action, or Automation operation) and rejects a fabricated manual-run case with `acceptance.workflow_manual_trigger_required`.

The scenario-level `expected_outcome` closed enum is `""`, `positive`, `exception`, or `denied` — nothing else. Use `positive` for an expected success, `denied` for an expected Runtime authorization denial, and `exception` for every other expected non-success (state-machine rejection, RLS concealment, business precondition failure). Do not confuse it with the different `config.runtime_operations[].expected_outcome` enum documented below; the two enums are validated independently and values are not interchangeable. A `denied` scenario's role must actually be unable to execute every attempted Action: the composer rejects a denied scenario whose role holds the Action's authorization (`compose.acceptance_denied_role_can_execute_action`) — pick a genuinely unauthorized role or remove the grant.

### Acceptance composition rules enforced by `project acceptance prepare`

The denominator builder enforces these composition rules; authoring scenarios without them costs one repair round each:

- **Requirement coverage**: every `requirement` item — including purely declarative ones such as acceptance provisioning or navigation — must be reachable from at least one `acceptance` item's `requirement_keys` whose scenarios produce executable cases (`acceptance.requirement_coverage_missing: <key> resources=N operations=0 cases=0` otherwise). Cases come only from `actions`/`attempted_actions`, `workflows`, `expected_reports`, and `config.runtime_operations`; a scenario carrying only `expected_records` produces no case.
- **Write denial coverage**: every write operation — each write Action and each write `runtime_operations` route — needs a denied-role case (`acceptance.permission_denial_missing`). For Actions, author a `denied` scenario with an unauthorized role. For typed routes, author a scenario whose `runtime_operations` entry sets **`"case": "permission_denied"`** (setting only `expected_outcome: denied` is not recognized); its default error code is `auth.permission_denied`, and its role must genuinely lack the route's required permissions.
- **Handler positive coverage is symmetric and DIRECT**: every Handler Action also needs a positive scenario whose `actions` list references it directly with an allowed role (`ledger.action_positive_scenario_missing`). Coverage through a Workflow branch that invokes the Handler does not count — a scheduler-driven or approval-driven Handler still needs one direct positive probe (e.g. the operator role invoking it with an explicit payload).
- **Every declared Object needs at least one seed** — including runtime-product objects such as reminder records or export audit/download artifacts (`ledger.seed_evidence_incomplete` names the missing objects); there is no exemption for objects normally populated only at runtime.
- Treat seed records as a closed typed graph before apply: every required field needs a value or declared default, every `$record:<seed-key>` relation must target a seed of the relation's declared object, option values must belong to the field value domain, and undeclared fields are errors. `model validate` reports these at the exact seed field; do not defer them to Runtime bootstrap.
- **Relation-typed `payload_fields` require `target_object_key`** referencing a **project** object; a Foundation target (e.g. an organization unit) is not resolvable there — pass the identifier as `text` and keep the Object field itself as the real relation.
- **Denied report cases are auto-derived — never author them.** A scenario referencing a report in `expected_reports` must use a role that IS allowed to read it (`acceptance.report_role_not_allowed` otherwise). For a protected report (non-empty `audience_roles`/`required_permissions`), the builder automatically finds an unauthorized role and emits the `permission_denied` case itself; it fails `acceptance.report_denied_role_missing` if no declared role is unauthorized. The same auto-derivation applies to Workflow denied cases.
- **CRUD/list/navigation coverage uses `config.runtime_operations` route keys** from the pinned Runtime Domain API `routes` map. The most-used keys: `object_query` (bounded list GET /objects/{objectKey}/records), `object_detail`, `object_create` (idempotency-key required), `object_update`, `object_delete`, `object_action`, `record_action`, `record_export`, `record_import_apply`, `effective_menu_list` (GET /identity/effective-menus), `business_notification_list`/`business_notification_stream` (SSE). Verify a key's readiness through `contract capability-category` before relying on it.
- **Prepare prerequisites**: a current verification receipt and a running healthy managed Runtime of the exact current cohort. Pass `--project` as an **absolute path** — a relative path currently fails the database-identity check with `managed Runtime database identity escapes the current project`.

Their nested shapes are closed too. `expected_records[]` accepts only `object_key`, `record_key`, `field_key`, `state`, `count`, and `values`; it has no `scope`. `expected_reports[]` accepts only `report_key`, `expected_run`, `expected_export`, `filters`, and array-valued `metrics` (use `[]`, not `{}`, when no metric is asserted). Assertions accept only their published typed assertion fields.

When a requirement consumes a typed Runtime capability that is not already represented by `actions`, `workflows`, or `expected_reports`, declare it under the scenario's `config.runtime_operations`. Each entry uses only `route_key` from the pinned Runtime Domain API plus optional `case`, `lifecycle`, `restart_sensitive`, `expected_outcome`, and `expected_error_code`; unknown fields, wrong field types, and route keys absent from the pinned Runtime Domain API fail during `model validate` (`evidence.typed_operation_route_unknown`). Use separate positive and `permission_denied` scenarios/roles for a write. The acceptance denominator resolves the route to the unified capability disclosure, preserves its real read/write effect class, required permissions, and SSE disposition, and rejects an allowed role labeled denied, a positive role missing the published permission, or a write without both positive and denied coverage. `expected_outcome`, when supplied, is one of `passed`, `denied`, `conflict`, `rejected`, `concealed`, `not_found`, or `failed`. For an SSE route, the case/lifecycle must be `sse_disconnect_resume`/`disconnect_resume` and `restart_sensitive` must be omitted or `false`: Last-Event-ID reconnect is not a managed process restart and requires only the stream transcript plus durable refetch. Do not reduce it to a connection-open check or attach unrelated restart/audit evidence.

```json
{"config": {
  "runtime_operations": [
    {"route_key":"business_notification_stream","case":"sse_disconnect_resume","lifecycle":"disconnect_resume"}
  ]
}}
```

A positive scenario's referenced seed records must already satisfy every source-owned Handler precondition needed for the expected success path. Every positive or denied role used by executable acceptance must have a project-declared `demo_users[]` identity. Bind a specific identity through `actor`; when an automatic standard case only has a role, that role must have exactly one demo user or exactly one user marked `acceptance_default:true`. The default applies across both `role_key` and `role_keys`; alphabetical order is never identity resolution. A role label alone is not a login. Keep separate negative business-precondition scenarios when that rejection matters. Denied authorization scenarios remain distinct and must fail at the Runtime authorization boundary.

When a positive Action needs a value the standard runner cannot derive, declare the runner-owned fixture in that scenario's open `config` map: `"action_payloads":[{"action_key":"<declared scenario action>","fields":{"<payload key>":{"value":<typed scalar>}}}]`. An omitted `encoding` requires a literal conforming exactly to the declared scalar payload type; relation/reference literals accept only `$record:<seed-key>` of the declared target, and user literals accept only `$actor`. The existing `{"encoding":"json","value":<array or object>}` form remains available only for `text`/`long_text`, resolving nested `$record:<seed-key>` values before canonical JSON encoding. The Action must belong to that positive scenario, actor plus Action must identify one scenario/role binding, and malformed, missing-seed, duplicate, or ambiguous fixtures fail closed; fixture fields are never conflict-mutation slots. Do not declare fixtures for values the standard type derivation already supplies.

Validation must close actor/role, object/relation, Action/authorization/data access, Automation/Workflow/Scheduler ownership, frontend entrypoints, and positive plus denied acceptance. Single-owner semantics and behavior shape tuples live in [behavior owner decision](capabilities/behavior-owner-decision.md).
